summary: iter316-E admin self-demotion safeguards + self-recovery — VERIFIED. All 8 review-request assertions PASS. Preview admin charbel911@gmail.com restored (role=admin, is_admin=true) and can access /api/twilio/admin/contractors (200). Both backend safeguards return 409 cannot_demote_admin with bilingual messages. Self-recovery endpoint correctly restores demoted admins, refuses privilege-escalation for users with previous_role!=admin, and 409s for already-admin / not-a-contractor / requires-auth states. Frontend dropdown safeguard in EnhancedUserManager.js correctly renders null (no 'Promote to Contractor' item) for admin/super_admin/is_admin users. Full iter316 regression: 56/56 pytest cases pass in 32.69s.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: admin_create_contractor (twilio.py ~810-845) and admin_promote_user (twilio.py ~895-905) previously had NO check preventing a target user with role=admin from being downgraded to dialer_contractor — so an admin clicking 'Promote to Contractor' on their own row would silently flip their own role to dialer_contractor and lock them out of the admin panel. FIX: (1) Both endpoints now early-return HTTP 409 detail.error=cannot_demote_admin (with bilingual messages) when target user.role in {admin, super_admin} or user.is_admin is true. (2) NEW POST /api/twilio/auth/restore-admin-role (twilio.py ~1428-1490) lets a logged-in user who was previously admin restore themselves IFF role==dialer_contractor AND previous_role in {admin, super_admin}; otherwise returns 403 not_eligible (prevents escalation) or 409 not_a_contractor (idempotent). (3) Frontend EnhancedUserManager.js:1105 renders null for the menu item when row user is admin (defensive UI guard). MITIGATION ON PROD: redeploy, then user calls the new recovery endpoint from their own logged-in session.
